description: Enterprise techniques used by Vidar, ATT&CK software S9050 (v1.0)
name: Vidar (S9050)

techniques.comment:
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has bypassed UAC by setting the Registry value `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\EnableLUA` to `0`, which disabled UAC.(Citation: Logpoint_Stealer 
MalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used HTTP/HTTPS to retrieve and send data and beacons.(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: CyberAus_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has performed dynamic DNS resolution for gz[.]technicalprorj[.]xyz via 8.8.8[.]8.(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has packaged collected data into a zip file before exfiltration.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has collected data using automated scripts within malicious executables.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has collected browser history from the victim machine.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used PowerShell commands to modify Windows Defender’s list of excluded file extensions.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has created the RegAsm.exe process in a suspended state.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has gathered credentials and data, including history, credit cards and auto-filled information, from decrypted browser files from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Opera, Vivaldi, Waterfox and Palemoon.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has attempted to collect browser information.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has compiled collected data into a randomly generated directory in the ProgramData folder.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the `IsDebuggerPresent` function to detect whether a debugger is present on a victim machine.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has waited for six seconds using the command `timeout /t 6`.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the function `CryptDecrypt`. Additionally, [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has decoded the .data section using bitwise XOR operations.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has decoded its core code after confirming debugger and/or analysis tools.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has modified Windows Defender’s list of excluded file extensions, ensuring that .exe, .dll and .bat files are ignored during scans.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024) 

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has loaded amsi.dll, which resolves the `AmsiScanBuffer` variable to return `E_INVALIDARG`, which may disable Windows Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI).(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been distributed via malicious advertisements when users searched for “Notepad++.”(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used TLS 1.2 for C2 communication.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

If a debugger or analysis environment is detected, [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has triggered a memory access violation exception, terminating its process by calling `RtlExitUserProcess`.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has exfiltrated sensitive data, such as credentials and cryptocurrency wallets, over the C2 server at 136.243.203[.]109.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has exfiltrated collected data through its C2 channel.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has gathered information about files on the victim machine.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026) Specifically, [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used `FindFirstFileExW` and `FindNextFileW`.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has attempted to read hidden system directories, such as `$Recycle.Bin`, `$Windows.~BT`, and `$SysReset`, and the `C:\Windows\System32\config\SOFTWARE` directory using the `ReadFile` function. [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also accessed internal streams, such as `$SDH`, and has read Jump Lists, which include recently opened files, programs and tasks.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used `icacls` to modify file permissions.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used a hidden directory in the ProgramData directory to store collected data.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been executed as a file named msedge_elf.dll through sideloading.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has self-deleted its initial executable to operate in memory.(Citation: CyberAus_Vidar_May2026) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has deleted collected data after exfiltration.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also deleted the file Malware.exe and all .dll files in the ProgramData folder using the command `del /f /q “C:\Users\MalWorkstation\Desktop\Malware.exe” &
del C:\ProgramData\*.dll`.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has downloaded additional binaries from the C2 server such as sqlx[1].dll, a sqlite3 binary for data harvesting and exfiltration.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also ownloaded get.zip, an archive containing several DLL libraries that extracted data from applications and browsers.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has signed its DLL using fake certificates githab[.]com and grow[.]com.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also signed its files with an expired digital certificate.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has masqueraded as a Microsoft Edge DLL.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has masqueraded as MicrosoftUpdate.exe in the %TEMP% folder.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has masqueraded as a Notepad++ installer named npp.Installer.x64.zip.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has masqueraded as an executable named Setup.exe that mimics the legitimate Yahtzee application.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has set the Registry value associated with User Access Control (UAC) (i.e. `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\EnableLUA`) to `0`, which disabled UAC.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used native Windows functions, such as `LoadLibraryExW`, for discovery and execution.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also used control flow flattening to slow down static analysis.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)

An AES-encrypted version of [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been embedded into an inflated executable named Setup.exe, bypassing defensive tools.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has obfuscated stack strings within executable files.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has obfuscated and/or AES-encrypted its core code to avoid debugger and/or analysis tools.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used XOR to obfuscate the DLL name and the function name with key 0x05 to evade static string scanning.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023) 

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has Base64-encoded information relating to cryptocurrency wallet extensions.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been distributed through emails that include malicious attachments, such as an ISO file, often masquerading as legitimate software, such as Adobe Photoshop or Microsoft Teams.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been distributed through emails that include malicious links that redirect to fake download pages for Adobe Illustrator.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the functions `GetCurrentProcess` and `GetCurrentProcessId` to obtain information about processes.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has injected itself into a legitimate Windows process.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has injected code into the suspended RegAsm.exe process.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used process hollowing to inject itself into an AppLaunch.exe process.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the function `TerminateProcess` to terminate processes.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has forcefully terminated a process named Devil.exe using the command `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe” /c taskkill /im Devil.exe /f`.(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has loaded and executed common Windows DLLs during execution.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has extracted session cookies.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has gathered hardware IDs (HWIDs) regarding the victim machine.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used `GetEnvironmentStringsW` and `GetModuleHandleExW` to gather information about the victim machine.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has collected OS data from the victim machine.(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the `EnumSystemLocalesW` function to enumerate installed or supported locales on the victim machine.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024) [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also used a GET request to ip-api[.]com, resolving the victim's public IP address and country.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has collected the victim's public IP address.(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has resumed the suspended process RegAsm.exe.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the `GetSystemTimeAsFileTime` function to retrieve the current system date and time of the victim machine.(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has collected credentials and cryptocurrency wallets stored internally.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: Unit42_Vidar_July2026)(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has also decrypted local file stores, such as key4.db for Firefox, to find credentials.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been distributed via a malicious link that redirects to a filesharing website.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used fake CAPTCHAs to deliver and execute itself to victims.(Citation: CyberAus_Vidar_May2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used 
`ZwQueryInformationProcess` to query process debug-related attributes, such as ProcessDebugPort and ProcessDebugFlags, and to query ProcessInstrumentationCallback (0x25) to evade analysis environments and monitoring tools.(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used the `Sleep` API before C2 communication.(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)

[Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has used Telegram and Steam dead drop resolvers to recover its C2 domain.(Citation: Intrinsec_Vidar_April2026)(Citation: LevelBlue_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: CyberAus_Vidar_May2026)(Citation: Cyfirma_Vidar_June2024)(Citation: Logpoint_StealerMalwareFamilies_2024)(Citation: QuorumCyber_Vidar_March2023)
